# Bāhiya Sutta (Ud 1.10 (PTS Ud 6))
**ID:** Ud 1.10 (PTS Ud 6)
**Section:** Udāna (ud)
**Collection:** Suttas-Early-2
**Title (Pali):** Bāhiya Sutta
**SuttaCentral:** https://suttacentral.net/ud1.10
**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/s0503m.mul0.xml

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The *Bāhiya Sutta* (Ud 1.10, PTS Ud 6) is the tenth and concluding discourse of the Bodhivagga in the *Udāna* [Ñāṇananda 1971]. The sutta recounts the meeting between the Buddha and the bark-cloth ascetic Bāhiya Dārucīriya, who urgently requests Dhamma instruction [Ñāṇananda 1971; Bruhacs 2008]. The Buddha delivers a terse instruction on training the mind in bare awareness without conceptual proliferation (*papañca*) or reification: in the seen there will be merely the seen, in the heard merely the heard, in the sensed merely the sensed, and in the cognized merely the cognized (*diṭṭhe diṭṭhamattaṁ bhavissati...*) [Ñāṇananda 1971; Shonin et al. 2015; Levman 2014]. By avoiding imputation or projection of an "I" or "self" onto sensory phenomena, one is neither "here," nor "there," nor "in between," bringing an end to suffering (*dukkha*) [Shonin et al. 2015; Levman 2014; Bruhacs 2008]. Upon receiving this succinct teaching, Bāhiya instantly attains full awakening (arahantship) [SuttaCentral; Ñāṇananda 1971; Anālayo 2017]. Shortly afterwards, Bāhiya suffers a sudden fatal accident; the Buddha instructs the monks to cremate his remains, erect a stūpa (*thūpa*), and utters the concluding verse of uplift (*udāna*) concerning the state of liberation beyond the elements, form, and formlessness [Ñāṇananda 1971].
While the specific narrative frame of Bāhiya's immediate awakening has no known direct parallel in other early canons [Anālayo 2017], the core doctrinal formula on sense perception is directly paralleled in the *Mālukyaputta Sutta* (SN 35.95) of the *Saḷāyatana Saṁyutta* [SuttaCentral; Gómez 1976; Wen 2011]. DharmaNexus matches confirm this close relationship, showing that Ud 1.10 shares its longest textual sequence (§8.2–8.10) with SN 35.95 (§95.10.1–95.10.8), while also recording substantial text reuse with the Vinaya Khandhakas (Kd 1, Kd 15, Kd 5), several *Aṅguttara Nikāya* chapters, and commentary works such as the *Udāna-aṭṭhakathā* and *Dhammapada-aṭṭhakathā* [DharmaNexus]. SuttaCentral also identifies verse parallels to the concluding stanza in the Sanskrit and Tibetan *Udānavarga* (UV 26; Uv Kg 26) and its Chinese translations (*Chu yao jing*, T 212.27; *Fa ji yao song jing*, T 213.26) [SuttaCentral]. Later canonical and paracanonical Pali texts mentioning Bāhiya include the *Bāhiyatthera-apadāna* (Tha-Ap 538) and the *Nettippakaraṇa* [SuttaCentral].
